line_checks.text_starts: 3. Palette: the agreed teal and cream palette.
- `reference.png` uses three opaque colors ... The exact hex values above are the measured reference colors.
Make a character family for a side-view game using PIXL. The family has two members: a scout and a medic.

criterion_comparisons.literal_delta: Adds 'single frame'; a single still sprite is the assignment's deliverable, so no valid alternative is excluded.
criterion_comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A 32 by 64 two-frame strip would fail; the brief asks for one character sprite, so that is correct.
A soft-edged sprite with alpha 128 pixels fails; the owner excluded it.

criterion_comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md line 13 names the palette by role; lines 32 to 36 record the measured hex values as observations.
criterion_comparisons.literal_delta: Narrows the role palette to three exact hex values and excludes any shade.
criterion_comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A sprite with a second, darker teal for a shadow keeps the owner's teal-and-cream roles but fails this check. That is why the check is a proposal owned by the specialist, not an owner rule.
criterion_comparisons.disposition: keep as proposal; owner may widen the set after seeing the sample

criterion_comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md line 11: the dark outline of reference.png.
criterion_comparisons.literal_delta: Adds 'continuous' and 'no un-outlined edge runs'. reference.png has a closed outline around the whole figure and reference-b.png is the explicitly not-chosen un-outlined version, so continuity is the observed meaning of the chosen treatment.
criterion_comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A selectively outlined sprite (outline only on the lower edges) keeps a dark outline colour but fails; the brief's wording 'the reference's dark outline' points at the continuous treatment, so this is kept, with the clause attributed to the reference observation.
criterion_comparisons.disposition: keep; the continuity clause rests on the reference, which the owner chose

criterion_comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md lines 11 to 15 and 20: outline, palette roles, side view and reference.png as style reference.
criterion_comparisons.authority_basis: owner requirement with an expert reading of 'blocky cluster scale'
criterion_comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A finely detailed scout with one-pixel texture everywhere keeps the colours and outline but would not sit beside the reference as one family; style matching is what the reference is for.
criterion_comparisons.disposition: keep; 'blocky cluster scale' is the visual reviewer's reading of matching the reference, not a numeric rule

criterion_comparisons.literal_delta: Adds 'light, mobile' and 'chosen scouting landmarks'; the specific landmarks live in the creative brief as proposals.
criterion_comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A heavily armoured scout would pass the owner's wording but fail the specialist reading; therefore the criterion is marked proposal and may be revised.
